_comment: Authoritative heavy-machine physics tuning shared by server simulation and client replay. Changing any value is a gameplay change: bump BUILD and ship a matching hosted server release.

heft._comment: Three-times enlarged hulls read as foam under 1 g. Bots fall under gravity_multiplier times arena gravity; launch and jump speeds scale by its square root so heights hold while hang time shrinks.

prediction._comment: Client input replay between snapshots. A grounded hull normally rests on its drive, so replay cancels gravity. Grounded also counts underside contact, so a hull launched or flipped while one edge still touches the floor is grounded but not held up: when the hull moves along its own up axis faster than support_release_speed (m/s), replay applies gravity and pivots the hull on its lowest corner, as Jolt does on the server. Driving on a slope moves along the surface, not along hull up. Client presentation only; the server does not replay.

contact._comment: Tracks carry the weight: while on its drive the hull has track_hull_friction against the arena (the drive model handles grip), and slope_hold_fraction of the downhill pull is cancelled by the tracks up to the grip limit, so tanks park and climb on hills. Off its drive (roof/side) the hull grinds with stranded_hull_friction (Jolt combines sqrt(hull * floor)). bot_contact_friction is explicit Coulomb friction between clashing hulls.

motor._comment: Multipliers over catalogue drive values. rolling_resistance_multiplier scales the released-throttle coast deceleration (motor controllers brake hard) so knocked hulls stop instead of sliding; brakes stay stronger than coasting.
motor._steering_comment: Below steering_direction_threshold m/s, throttle selects the steering direction; above it, signed ground-plane forward speed does. Neutral keeps differential pivot steering.

nitro._comment: Nitro is raw machine power: boosted acceleration and top speed carry an Atlas off a jump ramp onto a roof. Multipliers over the (already motor-scaled) drive values while nitro is held with throttle.

mass._comment: Heavier builds are slower: catalogue top speed is scaled by clamp(1 + (reference_mass - mass) * top_speed_per_kg, min_top_speed_factor, max_top_speed_factor). A build at reference_mass keeps its drive speed.

walker._comment: Four-legged walkers stand at WalkerDrive.RIDE_HEIGHT; holding crouch lowers the hull to crouch_ride_height (metres at the canonical factor-three scale, about the tracked Atlas ride height) and never sinks faster than crouch_lower_speed m/s so the stance spring cannot slam the hull into the floor. The six-legged Scorpion does not crouch.

impacts._comment: Scales over authored weapon impulses (m/s at equal mass). Rams add knock-back because Jolt hull contacts are plastic. The lifter applies no force while charging (hold 0 keeps the flipper low) and releases one violent launch with flip spin.
impacts._pin_comment: Wall pin: a rammed bot that touches static arena geometry on its far side (within ram_pin_window_seconds of the ram) takes one crushing hit on the face the rammer struck. Damage depends only on the rammer: (base + per_speed * (its own speed into the victim - min_attacker_speed), capped at max) * clamp(its mass / mass.reference_mass, min_mass_factor, max_mass_factor). A rammer slower than min_attacker_speed (e.g. the bot that was rammed) pins nobody. Armour on that face stops at most ram_pin_armour_share of it; the rest reaches the core. Wall contacts are those whose normal has |y| below ram_pin_wall_max_normal_y, lying on the far side (horizontal alignment with the ram direction at least ram_pin_far_side_min_alignment).
